name: N-Acetyl Selank Amidate

lead: N-Acetyl Selank Amidate is a chemically modified version of the peptide Selank, with changes meant to help it resist breakdown and last longer in the body. Users hope for a calmer mood and more social ease than the parent peptide gives.

The chain is indirect: less anxiety and stress, a calmer and more composed demeanour, and better social presence. It is presumed to act like Selank, which is described as modulating GABAergic signalling. No studies of this exact compound are reported, and the benefits are extrapolated from Selank research.

paras: It is sold by research-chemical suppliers for laboratory use. Users describe it as a longer-lasting alternative to Selank, with no established routine or timeline.
It is not approved for human use in most jurisdictions. Safety in people has not been studied.

angle.text: This acetylated, amidated Selank analogue is sold as a research chemical, with users hoping for less anxiety, a calmer demeanour and more social ease. The link to looks runs through composure and presence. The analogue itself has no direct studies; the research relates to Selank.

lead: N-Acetyl Selank Amidate, sold as Adalank or NA-Selank, is a synthetic heptapeptide analog of Selank with the sequence Ac-Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro-NH2, acetylated at the N-terminus and amidated at the C-terminus. [1] These two changes are standard peptide-chemistry strategies described as intended to make the molecule resist enzymatic breakdown and last longer than Selank itself. [1]

Selank, the parent peptide, is a Russian-developed nootropic and anxiolytic related to the immune peptide tuftsin. [2] Interest in this analog comes from Selank's reported effects on anxiety, stress and cognition; no appearance use has been documented, and any link to looks would be indirect, through stress and mood. [1][2]

The variant is sold by research-chemical suppliers for laboratory use and is not approved for human therapeutic use. [1] No published study of this exact compound was located, and claimed benefits are extrapolated from research on Selank. [1]
infobox: Selank, developed at the Russian Academy of Sciences' Institute of Molecular Genetics [2]
Research chemical; not approved for human use [1]

paras: The acetyl group at the N-terminus is described as blocking aminopeptidases, and the amide at the C-terminus as blocking carboxypeptidases, which could extend plasma half-life and in vivo retention without changing the core sequence. [1] These stability benefits are described as hypothesized and unverified for this specific compound. [1]

Selank is a heptapeptide with the sequence Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro, a synthetic analog of human tuftsin, developed by the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences and closely related to Semax. [2] Wikipedia says it is available in Russian and Ukrainian pharmacies and that clinical studies examined its effects on cognition and anxiety, including comparisons with benzodiazepines, but that most mechanistic findings come from rodents. [2]

Reported mechanisms include immunomodulation through IL-6 and T helper cytokines, changes in monoamine levels, raised BDNF expression in rat hippocampus and inhibition of enzymes that break down enkephalins. [2] Grokipedia describes a clinical study of 62 patients with generalized anxiety disorder and neurasthenia in which Selank showed anxiolytic effects similar to medazepam. [1]

The variant is described as vendor-driven, created within the research chemical market to address the parent peptide's rapid degradation. [1] It is sold for laboratory use and is not approved by the FDA or in most jurisdictions for human consumption. [1]
No studies found of N-Acetyl Selank Amidate. Any clinical or animal findings relate to unmodified Selank, not this variant. [1][2]
